oarfish: A scientific field-guide illustration of an oarfish lying HORIZONTALLY ACROSS THE PICTURE in strict flat side profile, head at the left. ITS BODY IS AN EXTREMELY LONG NARROW SILVER STRAP, at least THIRTY TIMES LONGER THAN IT IS DEEP, of even depth for most of its length and tapering to a fine point at the far right where it simply ends. Along that length it swings through THREE DEEP SMOOTH UNDULATIONS, rising and falling well above and below the midline so the whole animal reads as a slow travelling wave. A CRIMSON FIN OF FINE CLOSE-SET RAYS RUNS THE ENTIRE LENGTH OF ITS BACK from just behind the head to the tip, unbroken. From the top of its small blunt head rises a TALL CREST OF SIX LONG CRIMSON PLUMES, each about twice the depth of the body. Two very long slender crimson pelvic fins trail back beneath it, each ending in a small flat blade. Silvery skin flecked with irregular dark grey spots and short dark bars, one large dark eye, and a small protrusible mouth.
nicobarpigeon: A scientific field-guide illustration of a Nicobar pigeon perched on a branch in three-quarter view, head to the left. A heavy-bodied pigeon whose head, throat and upper neck are PLAIN SLATE BLUE-GREY. From the nape and shoulders hang LONG POINTED HACKLE FEATHERS, each a separate narrow blade lying over the next, forming a shaggy cape down the neck and across the shoulders; these hackles run COPPER-ORANGE AND GOLD at the neck and shade into METALLIC EMERALD GREEN over the back and wings, every feather edged with its own bright highlight. THE TAIL IS SHORT AND PURE WHITE, a clean blunt white block at the rear, sharply cut off from the dark green body in front of it. A stout black bill with a rounded knob at its base, a dark eye, and short crimson legs with red feet.
sunflowerstar: A scientific field-guide illustration of a sunflower sea star seen from DIRECTLY ABOVE, lying flat on rock. IT HAS ABOUT TWENTY ARMS. They radiate all the way round a very wide soft central disc, and their bases are packed so closely that they touch one another and form a continuous ring with no gaps. EACH ARM IS THICK, SOFT AND FLESHY, roughly as wide at its base as one fifth of the disc, only about as long as the disc is wide, and tapering to a blunt rounded tip - a short plump limb rather than a slender ray. The arms curve gently and lie at slightly different angles rather than radiating in a rigid star. The whole animal is a deep orange, the skin loose and covered all over in short soft blunt knobbed spines.
opossum: A scientific field-guide illustration of a Virginia opossum standing on all four feet in three-quarter view, facing the viewer. Its body is covered in LONG COARSE GRIZZLED FUR, pale grey-white with darker guard hairs standing through it so the coat looks shaggy and untidy. THE FACE IS CLEAN WHITE from the brow down over the cheeks and chin, tapering to a NARROW POINTED SNOUT ending in a BRIGHT PINK NOSE. Its eyes are small, round and glossy black. ITS EARS ARE BARE BLACK LEATHERY OVALS with pink at the tips, standing out from the sides of the head. Long white whiskers spray from the muzzle. Its lower legs and feet are dark, ending in PINK TOES with pale claws, and a long thick bare pale tail trails behind.
frilledshark: A scientific field-guide illustration of a frilled shark's head and forebody in side profile, mouth open, head to the left. THE HEAD IS THE POINT. It is BROAD AND FLATTENED and ends in a BLUNT SQUARED FRONT: the whole face is cut off vertically at the tip so the MOUTH OPENS AT THE VERY FRONT OF THE ANIMAL, its jaw line running straight across the leading edge, and there is nothing projecting in front of or above it. The skin over the head and jaws is soft grey-brown and finely WRINKLED IN MANY CLOSE PARALLEL CREASES that run back along the body. The open mouth shows PALE PINK GUMS set with small widely spaced needle-sharp three-pronged teeth. Its eye is a bright GLASSY GREEN OVAL set low and far forward on the side of the head, and a small round spiracle sits behind it. Immediately behind, SIX RUFFLED GILL SLITS with loose frilled fringed edges.
scalyfootsnail: A scientific field-guide illustration of a scaly-foot snail in side view, shell uppermost and foot below, head to the right. ITS SHELL IS A LOW BROAD SPIRAL of dark iron grey with a dull metallic sheen, the whorls marked by fine close growth lines. BENEATH IT THE FOOT IS ARMOURED: HUNDREDS OF SMALL OVERLAPPING BLACK MINERAL SCALES cover the entire side and underside of the foot, each scale a flat rounded plate lying over the next in tight rows so the foot reads as a dense dark mail. Between the shell and the armour the soft body shows as GLOSSY SALMON PINK-RED flesh, and from the front two SLENDER PINK TENTACLES reach forward and curl.
gulpereel: A scientific field-guide illustration of a gulper eel in side profile, head to the left. ITS MOUTH IS ENORMOUS AND IS MOST OF THE ANIMAL: the lower jaw is a HUGE LOOSE POUCH-LIKE SCOOP hinged far back behind the tiny eye and hanging wide open, so long that it measures ABOUT ONE THIRD OF THE WHOLE ANIMAL, with the thin upper jaw of the same length lying above it. Both jaw rims carry a comb of many tiny fine teeth. The head itself is tiny and the eye is a minute dot right at the snout tip. Behind the jaws the body narrows abruptly into a VERY LONG THIN WHIP-LIKE TAIL that trails away and curls upward at the end, tapering to a fine thread tipped with a SMALL PALE PINK KNOB. Smooth dark blue-black skin with a faint violet sheen.
commonfangtooth: A scientific field-guide illustration of a common fangtooth in strict side profile, head to the left. A SHORT DEEP HEAVY-BODIED FISH, only about twice as long as it is deep, tapering sharply to a narrow tail stock. ITS HEAD IS ENORMOUS, taking up nearly HALF THE WHOLE LENGTH, blunt and steep-fronted with deep hollows and bony ridges above the jaw. THE MOUTH IS HELD OPEN AND THE TEETH ARE THE POINT: two ENORMOUS CURVED FANGS rise from the front of the lower jaw, each one as long as the eye is wide, standing up past the upper jaw, with smaller needle teeth in rows behind them. Its eye is small, pale and set high on the head. The skin is dark chocolate-brown to black, rough and finely pitted. Thin translucent fins with fine rays along the back, belly and forked tail.
viperfish: A scientific field-guide illustration of a viperfish in side profile, head to the left, its long body curving in one loose shallow bend. A SLENDER DARK SILVERY-GREEN FISH with large thin overlapping scales that give the flanks a faint honeycomb pattern. ITS TEETH ARE THE POINT: the jaws carry a few VERY LONG THIN NEEDLE FANGS that are TOO LONG TO CLOSE INSIDE THE MOUTH and stand outside it, the lower ones curving up past the eye. FROM ITS BACK JUST BEHIND THE HEAD RISES ONE ENORMOUSLY ELONGATED FIN RAY, a single bare filament that arches forward over the head and ends in a small pale tip well in front of the snout. Rows of tiny round PEARLY PHOTOPHORES run in neat lines along the belly and lower flank. A dark eye, small paired fins, and a small forked tail.
macropinnabarreleye: A scientific field-guide illustration of a barreleye in side profile, head to the right. THE FRONT OF ITS HEAD IS A LARGE COMPLETELY TRANSPARENT DOME, a smooth clear fluid-filled helmet through which the inside of the head is plainly visible. INSIDE THAT DOME SIT TWO BRIGHT EMERALD-GREEN BARREL-SHAPED EYES, each a short glowing green cylinder standing on end and AIMED STRAIGHT UPWARD through the top of the dome. AT THE FRONT OF THE FACE, BELOW AND IN FRONT OF THE DOME, ARE TWO SMALL DARK NOSTRIL PITS and a small mouth - these sit where eyes would be expected and are not eyes. Behind the clear head the body is short, dark and stout, ending in a small tail, with BROAD FLAT PALE FINS held out flat and horizontal to either side.
silverhatchetfish: A scientific field-guide illustration of a silver hatchetfish in strict side profile, head to the right. ITS BODY IS A DEEP THIN BLADE OF BURNISHED SILVER, very tall and strongly flattened side to side, DEEPEST AT THE CHEST just behind the head and sweeping down and back to a narrow tail stock, so the outline reads as a broad triangle with its point at the rear. The silver flanks are mirror-bright and iridescent with faint pink and blue sheens. ITS EYES ARE VERY LARGE, dark and set high on the head, LOOKING UPWARD. Along the lower edge of the belly runs a ROW OF SHORT SQUARE PHOTOPHORES set close together in one even line, dull and unpolished, and a second line runs along the flank. A small mouth angled upward, thin translucent fins, and a small dark forked tail.
marianasnailfish: A scientific field-guide illustration of a Mariana snailfish resting on pale sediment, seen from ABOVE AND SLIGHTLY BEHIND, head to the right. IT HAS NO SCALES AND ITS WHOLE BODY IS PALE TRANSLUCENT PINKISH-WHITE, soft and slightly gelatinous, so faint internal shadows show through the skin. ITS HEAD IS BROAD, ROUNDED AND FLATTENED, wider than the body behind it, with TWO TINY DARK EYE DOTS set far apart on top and a small wide mouth at the front. Behind the head the body narrows steadily into a slender tapering tail. TWO BROAD FAN-SHAPED PECTORAL FINS spread out flat to either side just behind the head, each spread wide with fine rays showing through the membrane, and a low soft fin runs along the tail to its blunt tip.
cookiecuttershark: A scientific field-guide illustration of a cookiecutter shark in side profile, head to the left. A SMALL SLENDER CIGAR-SHAPED SHARK with smooth milk-chocolate brown skin. AROUND ITS THROAT, JUST BEHIND THE HEAD, RUNS A BROAD DARK CHOCOLATE COLLAR, a distinct band encircling the neck and clearly darker than the body on either side of it. ITS MOUTH IS A SMALL ROUND SUCKING DISC at the front of the blunt snout, with THICK FLESHY LIPS and a single row of BROAD FLAT TRIANGULAR TEETH in the lower jaw, each tooth wide at the base and interlocking with the next. Its eye is LARGE AND BRIGHT GREEN with a dark slit pupil, set forward on the side of the head. Small fins set far back near the tail, each with a PALE WHITE MARGIN.
glacierlanternfish: A scientific field-guide illustration of a glacier lanternfish in strict side profile, head to the right. A SMALL SLENDER FISH about five times longer than it is deep, its flanks covered in large thin silvery scales tinged brown along the back and pale below. ITS EYE IS VERY LARGE AND ROUND, taking up most of the short blunt head, dark with a bright silver-blue ring. THE PHOTOPHORES ARE THE POINT: NEAT ROWS OF SMALL ROUND PALE BLUE-WHITE LIGHT ORGANS run along the underside of the body from chin to tail and in a second broken line low along the flank, each one a small raised bead catching the light. A small upturned mouth, a single soft dorsal fin at the middle of the back, a tiny adipose fin behind it, and a deeply forked translucent tail.
